titleEn: Dublin event on methane hears push back on Bovaer scepticism
titleZh: 都柏林甲烷会议为Bovaer争议辩护
summaryZh: 都柏林一场由EDF组织的甲烷排放会议聚焦反刍动物饲料添加剂Bovaer（3-NOP），多位发言人为其安全性和减排效果辩护，指出公众认知与科学证据之间存在鸿沟，强调需要加强科普教育。此前丹麦部分农户报告奶牛健康与产奶量受影响，EFSA正在审查相关数据。荷兰FrieslandCampina已推行Bovaer约三年且无农户投诉。
featuredReason: Bovaer作为全球最受关注的减甲烷饲料添加剂，其科学争议与公众认知的博弈直接影响反刍动物养殖的减排路径和消费者信任，智慧畜牧从业者需关注这一议题对精准饲喂和牧场管理技术推广的潜在影响。
contentFull: Top Stories Beef Dairy Sheep Tillage Machinery Northern Ireland Videos Podcasts Top Stories Beef Dairy Sheep Tillage Machinery Northern Ireland Videos Podcasts Dublin event on methane hears push back on Bovaer scepticism ![Image 1: Charles O'Donnell By Charles O'Donnell September 24, 2026 6:14 PM](https:www.agriland.iefarming-newsauthorcharles) Share this article ![Image 2](https:www.agriland.iefarming-newsdublin-event-on-methane-hears-push-back-on-bovaer-scepticism) A conference in Dublin on methane emissions from livestock has heard push back against claims made about the feed additive Bovaer. The conference, organised by the international climate advocacy group Environmental Defence Fund (EDF), saw a wide ranging conversation, including on livestock feed additives that can reduce methane emissions from cows. This comes as the European Food Safety Authority (EFSA) is completing a scientific opinion on Bovaer, the most widely-known methane-cutting feed additive. Earlier this year, the EFSA launched a review into the use of 3-nitrooxypropanol (3-NOP), which is sold as Bovaer, in dairy cows and cows for breeding. The European Commission had asked the EFSA to provide the scientific opinion on the safety of the methane-reducing feed ingredient. The request followed reports from some farmers in Denmark that their cows' health and milk output had been impacted after using Bovaer. However, no scientific link between Bovaer and negative impacts on cow health or milk yield is known to exist at present. Bovaer was mentioned - or alluded to - several times at the conference in the RDS in Dublin today (Thursday, September 24). The event, which was titled 'On-Farm Solutions: New Opportunities For Business Cases', heard from several speakers from Ireland's agri-sector. These included Sean McCarthy, on-farm sustainability manager with Kinisla. McCarthy said: "Well I suppose this is where science and perception kind of meet... There’s plenty of science to support that [Bovaer] is safe to use and is effective in terms of reducing methane. "So the issue we have, and you’ve seen it a number of times now, is where 'soundbites' in the different platforms and within the public arena are creating almost an uncertainty, or scaring our consumers. So there’s a huge education piece to happen there," McCarthy added. "So I think education will be hugely important. I think we need to be creative there. "It's almost a kind of a psychology piece really in terms of supporting the science. So we do need science, but science ends up in peer-reviewed journals, which the vast majority of people don’t read," McCarthy stated. Another speaker at the event, Saskia Visser from Climate KIC, the Netherlands-based climate innovation agency, noted that Dutch dairy company FrieslandCampina has been incentivising its suppliers to use Bovaer for around three years, without any complaints from farmers in that time. Asking a question from the floor, John Harrison from the research division of the Department of Agriculture, Food and the Marine also touched on Bovaer and feed additives generally. He said that the conversation around feed additives has been "distracted" somewhat by the Bovaer issue, but he also said that it is "the most widely-researched feed additive in the world, and has been shown to be safe". Harrison asked if there was a responsibility on stakeholders to combat what he said was "misinformation possibly" around the product. translationZh:
一场在都柏林举行的关于牲畜甲烷排放的会议，听到了对有关饲料添加剂Bovaer说法的反驳。

这场会议由国际气候倡导组织环境保护基金（EDF）组织，围绕 livestock 饲料添加剂展开了广泛讨论，这些添加剂可减少奶牛的甲烷排放。

与此同时，欧洲食品安全局（EFSA）正在完成关于Bovaer的科学意见，Bovaer是最广为人知的减甲烷饲料添加剂。今年早些时候，EFSA启动了对3-硝基氧基丙醇（3-NOP，以Bovaer名称销售）在奶牛和繁殖母牛中使用情况的审查。

欧盟委员会此前要求EFSA就这种减甲烷饲料成分的安全性提供科学意见。这一要求是在丹麦部分农户报告其奶牛在使用Bovaer后健康和产奶量受到影响之后提出的。

然而，目前尚无已知的科学证据表明Bovaer与奶牛健康或产奶量负面影响之间存在关联。

在今天（9月24日星期四）于都柏林RDS举行的会议上，Bovaer被多次提及或暗示。这场活动题为“农场解决方案：商业案例的新机遇”，听取了多位来自爱尔兰农业领域的发言人的意见。

其中包括Kinisla的农场可持续发展经理Sean McCarthy。McCarthy表示：“嗯，我想这正是科学与认知交汇的地方……有大量科学证据支持[Bovaer]使用安全，并且在减少甲烷方面有效。”

“所以我们面临的问题是，你们现在已经多次看到，不同平台和公共领域中的‘片段式言论’几乎在制造不确定性，或者吓唬我们的消费者。所以这里需要做大量的教育工作，”McCarthy补充道。

“所以我认为教育将非常重要。我认为我们需要在这方面有创意。”

“这几乎真的是一种心理学层面的工作，用来支持科学。我们确实需要科学，但科学最终发表在同行评审期刊上，而绝大多数人不会去读，”McCarthy表示。

会议的另一位发言人是来自荷兰气候创新机构Climate KIC的Saskia Visser，她指出荷兰乳企FrieslandCampina约三年来一直在激励其供应商使用Bovaer，在此期间没有收到农户的任何投诉。

农业、食品和海洋部研究部门的John Harrison在观众提问环节也谈到了Bovaer和饲料添加剂的一般问题。他说，围绕饲料添加剂的讨论在某种程度上被Bovaer问题“分散了注意力”，但他也表示，它是“世界上研究最广泛的饲料添加剂，并已被证明是安全的”。

Harrison询问，利益相关者是否有责任打击他所说的围绕该产品的“可能是错误信息”。
